sources.note: Describes KWAIO (Sinalagu/'Xwaio' dialect), not Dori'o. §1.2.2 Stress, pp. 9-11: 'Stress within morphemes is, with few exceptions, placed on the penultimate vowel. Stress is somewhat heavier on the penultimate vowel of the final segment of a polymorphemic form.' Exceptions: CVV verb bases + monosyllabic object suffix do not shift stress; unanalysable trisyllables get roughly equal stress on the first two vowels; analysable trisyllables have penultimate primary + initial secondary stress. The latter two dialects.. manifest most of the sound shifts in the direction of 'Are'are'; Keesing used a Kwarekwareo informant in 1970 but gives no Dori'o phonology. Vowel table p. xv notes /e/ = [e:] unstressed, [e] stressed (Kwaio); no placement rule.
